title: Big ears
q: British clubs that won the European Cup or Champions League, up to 2025
rule: Finals from 1956 to 2025 only; Cup Winners' Cup, UEFA Cup and Europa League wins do not count.
fact: Nottingham Forest won the European Cup in 1979 and 1980, yet have been champions of England only once, in 1977-78.

traps.Rangers: Their only European trophy is the 1972 Cup Winners' Cup.
traps.Aberdeen: Won the 1983 Cup Winners' Cup, not the European Cup.

title: Host nations
q: Hosts of the men's football World Cup, from 1930 to 2026
rule: Every co-host counts, and Cold War-era states count under their modern names.
fact: Colombia withdrew as 1986 hosts, so Mexico stepped in and became the first country to host the men's World Cup twice; 2026 gave it a record third.

traps.Colombia: Awarded the 1986 tournament but withdrew, and Mexico took over.
traps.Portugal: Hosted Euro 2004, not a World Cup.
traps.Australia: Co-hosted only the 2023 Women's World Cup.
traps.China: Hosted the Women's World Cup, not the men's.

title: One and done
q: Retired F1 drivers who won the world title exactly once
rule: Drivers' titles from 1950 to 2025. Hill and Rosberg appear twice, so give a first name.
fact: Jochen Rindt is the only posthumous F1 champion: he was killed at Monza in September 1970 and no rival could overhaul his points lead.

traps.Stirling Moss: Runner-up four years running (1955-58) but never champion.
traps.Gilles Villeneuve: Never champion; Jacques's father was runner-up in 1979.
traps.Felipe Massa: Lost the 2008 title to Lewis Hamilton by a single point.
traps.Lando Norris: Champion in 2025 but still racing, so not counted here.

title: Home turf
q: Ballon d'Or winners who won it while playing for an English club
rule: Men's winners 1956 to 2025, judged by the club in the award year. Plain "Ronaldo" is taken as Cristiano.
fact: Stanley Matthews won the first Ballon d'Or in 1956 at the age of 41, while at Blackpool, and is still the oldest winner.

traps.Kevin Keegan: Won in 1978 and 1979 while playing for Hamburg in Germany.
traps.Luis Suárez: The 1960 winner was a Spaniard at Barcelona; the Liverpool striker never won.

title: Class of '92
q: Clubs that played in the first Premier League season, 1992-93
rule: The 22 clubs that kicked off in August 1992; clubs promoted a year later do not count.
fact: Brian Deane's goal for Sheffield United against Manchester United on 15 August 1992 was the first in Premier League history.

traps.Newcastle United: Won the second tier in 1992-93 and joined a year later.
traps.West Ham United: Promoted in 1993, so their first season was 1993-94.
traps.Leicester City: Only reached the Premier League in 1994, via the play-offs.
traps.Sunderland: Stayed in the second tier until 1996.
traps.Derby County: Stayed in the second tier until 1996.

title: Founding fathers
q: Founder members of the Football League in 1888
rule: The 12 clubs of the first season, 1888-89. The defunct original club from a Lancashire town counts, not its modern successor.
fact: Accrington FC dropped out of the league in 1893 and folded within three years; today's Accrington Stanley is an entirely separate club.

traps.Sunderland: Elected in 1890, after the League began.

title: Not the capital
q: Summer Olympic host cities that aren't national capitals
rule: Games from 1896 to 2024. 'Capital' means a sovereign country's capital today, so a former capital counts as not a capital.
fact: Melbourne 1956 was the first Games in the Southern Hemisphere, but the equestrian events were held in Stockholm because of Australian quarantine rules.

traps.Chicago: Bid for 2016 but lost out to Rio; never hosted.
traps.Istanbul: Bid several times but has never hosted.
traps.Amsterdam: It is the capital of the Netherlands.

title: Golden touch
q: Premier League top scorers of the season, 1992-93 to 2024-25
rule: Anyone who won or shared the Golden Boot in those 33 seasons.
fact: Three-way ties for the Golden Boot came in 1997-98 (Owen, Sutton and Dublin, all on 18), in 1998-99 and in 2018-19.

traps.Ian Wright: Never won the Golden Boot, despite scoring heavily for Arsenal.
traps.Wayne Rooney: Scored 208 Premier League goals but never finished top.
traps.Robbie Fowler: Never top; Shearer pipped him in 1995-96.
traps.Eric Cantona: Never finished as the league's top scorer.
traps.Frank Lampard: Never finished as the league's top scorer.

title: Show your hand
q: A ranked hand in standard five-card poker
rule: Standard 52-card deck with no wild cards. Every named ranking counts separately, including the very best.
fact: Only 4 of the 2,598,960 possible five-card hands are royal flushes, while about half of all hands are just High Card.

traps.Five of a Kind: Needs a wild card; impossible with a standard deck.
traps.Three Pair: Needs six cards; a five-card hand holds two pairs at most.
traps.Dead Man's Hand: Aces and eights is a famous two pair, not a ranking.
traps.Flush Draw: A draw is an unfinished hand, not a ranked one.

title: Old school
q: Pokémon types that existed in the first generation of games
rule: The 15 types in Red, Green, Blue and Yellow; Dark, Steel and Fairy came later.
fact: Ghost moves were meant to be super effective against Psychic types, but a bug in Red and Blue made them do no damage at all.

traps.Dark: Added in Gold and Silver in 1999.
traps.Steel: Added in Gold and Silver in 1999.
traps.Fairy: Added much later, in X and Y in 2013.

title: Crucible kings
q: World Snooker champions crowned at the Crucible, 1977 to 2025
rule: Winners from 1977 to 2025. Higgins appears twice (Alex and John), so give a first name; earlier champions do not count.
fact: Cliff Thorburn, from Canada, was the Crucible's first overseas champion in 1980; Zhao Xintong became the first Chinese world champion in 2025.

traps.Joe Davis: Won 15 world titles, all between 1927 and 1946.
traps.Fred Davis: Won his world titles before the Crucible era began in 1977.
traps.Jimmy White: Lost six Crucible finals and never won the title.

title: Shire power
q: First-class cricket counties in the County Championship
rule: The 18 first-class counties; Minor Counties sides such as Devon and Norfolk do not count.
fact: Durham joined the County Championship only in 1992, yet had won it by 2008 and added titles in 2009 and 2013.

traps.Devon: A Minor Counties side, not first-class.
traps.Cornwall: A Minor Counties side, not first-class.
traps.Norfolk: A Minor Counties side, not first-class.
traps.Berkshire: A Minor Counties side, not first-class.
traps.Cambridgeshire: A Minor Counties side, not first-class.

title: Badge of honour
q: Teams that have won the F1 Constructors' Championship, up to 2024
rule: Count the constructor's title, not the driver's, and only titles won by the team itself up to the 2024 season.
fact: Brawn GP won both the 2009 drivers' and constructors' titles in its only season, after Honda pulled out and Ross Brawn bought the team.

traps.Jordan: Jordan never won the constructors' title; its best finish was third.
traps.Toyota: Toyota ran its own works team for years and never won a title.
traps.Sauber: Sauber never won the constructors' title.

title: Animal house
q: NFL teams whose nickname is a real animal
rule: The nickname must name a single animal. The Seahawks do not count.
fact: The Baltimore Colts left town overnight in March 1984 for Indianapolis, where the name has been used ever since.

traps.Chicago Bulls: The Bulls are an NBA team, not an NFL one.
traps.Detroit Tigers: The Tigers are a baseball team. Detroit's NFL team is the Lions.
traps.Wolves: No NFL team is called the Wolves.

title: Home advantage
q: Countries that have hosted a Rugby World Cup, up to 2023
rule: Any country that staged matches as a host or co-host counts, up to 2023.
fact: Japan became the first Asian country to host a Rugby World Cup in 2019.

traps.United States: The USA has never hosted a Rugby World Cup.
traps.Argentina: Argentina has never been a named host.

title: Original six
q: Sports on the programme at Chamonix 1924, the first Winter Olympics
rule: Count the sport, not each event. A sport that goes by a second name also counts under that name.
fact: Chamonix 1924 was first called the International Winter Sports Week and was only retrospectively given Olympic status.

traps.Alpine skiing: Alpine skiing was first held at the Winter Games in 1936.
traps.Biathlon: Biathlon was first held at the Winter Games in 1960.
traps.Snowboarding: Snowboarding was first held at the Winter Games in 1998.

title: Never on top
q: Premier League clubs that have never won the English top-flight title
rule: Any of the 28 clubs that played in the Premier League from 1992-93 to 2025-26 and have never won the top-flight title (including the old First Division) up to 2024-25.
fact: Southampton have never won the top-flight title, but they beat Manchester United 1-0 in the 1976 FA Cup final.

traps.Newcastle United: Newcastle have won the old First Division more than once.
traps.Everton: Everton have won the top-flight title more than once.
traps.Leeds United: Leeds won the top-flight title in 1992.

title: Cup holders
q: Clubs that won the FA Cup in the Premier League era, 1993 to 2024
rule: Any club that won an FA Cup final from 1993 to 2024 inclusive. Finals decided on penalties count as wins.
fact: Wigan Athletic won the 2013 FA Cup 1-0 against Manchester City, and were relegated from the Premier League that same season.

traps.Tottenham Hotspur: Spurs' last FA Cup win was in 1991, before the Premier League began.
traps.Aston Villa: Villa lost the 2015 final 4-0 to Arsenal.
traps.Newcastle United: Newcastle lost the 1998 final 2-0 to Arsenal.

title: Never went down
q: Clubs never relegated from the Premier League, up to 2024-25
rule: Any club that has played in the Premier League and has never been relegated from it, based on results up to the end of 2024-25.
fact: Everton have never been relegated from the Premier League, and their last relegation from the top flight came in 1951.

traps.Newcastle United: Newcastle went down from the Premier League in 2009.
traps.Manchester City: Relegated from the Premier League in 1995-96.

title: Links legends
q: Scottish courses that have hosted The Open Championship
rule: Any Scottish course that has hosted The Open, past or present, up to 2025.
fact: The first Open was played at Prestwick in 1860, and it was won by Willie Park Sr.

traps.Royal Liverpool: Royal Liverpool hosts The Open, but it is in England.
traps.Royal Portrush: Royal Portrush hosts The Open, but it is in Northern Ireland.
traps.Gleneagles: Gleneagles is a Scottish resort course, but it has never hosted The Open.

title: Final stage
q: Teams that have played in a men's Cricket World Cup final, up to 2023
rule: Any team that has reached a men's ODI World Cup final up to 2023. Losing finalists count as well as winners.
fact: New Zealand lost both of their World Cup finals, in 2015 to Australia and in 2019 to England after a super-over tie.

traps.South Africa: South Africa have never reached a Cricket World Cup final.
traps.Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe have never reached a Cricket World Cup final.
traps.Ireland: Ireland have never reached a Cricket World Cup final.

title: Wide world
q: F1 world champions born outside Europe
rule: Judged by country of birth, not nationality or racing base. Any driver crowned champion from 1950 to 2025.
fact: Juan Manuel Fangio won five world titles, and he was born in Argentina.

traps.Michael Schumacher: Schumacher was born in Germany, which is in Europe.
traps.Lewis Hamilton: Hamilton was born in Stevenage, England.
traps.Mario Andretti: Andretti was born in Italy, which is in Europe.

title: City slickers
q: Premier League clubs whose name ends in City
rule: Any club that has played in the Premier League from 1992-93 to 2025-26 and whose official name ends with the word City.
fact: Leicester City won the 2015-16 Premier League title at odds of 5000-1 before the season began.

traps.Bristol City: Bristol City have never played in the Premier League.
traps.Oxford United: Oxford United have never played in the Premier League, and their name does not end in City.
traps.Derby County: Derby played in the Premier League, but their name does not end in City.

title: Repeat offenders
q: Clubs that have won the European Cup or Champions League twice or more
rule: Count only titles won in the European Cup or Champions League, up to the 2025 final. Every title counts, not just the most recent.
fact: Real Madrid won the first five European Cups between 1956 and 1960.

traps.Arsenal: Arsenal have never won the European Cup or Champions League, though they won the Cup Winners' Cup.
traps.Celtic: Celtic won the European Cup once, in 1967.
traps.Borussia Dortmund: Dortmund won the European Cup once, in 1997.
traps.Manchester City: City won the Champions League for the first time in 2023.

title: Single file
q: Letters worth just one point in English Scrabble
rule: Blank tiles score nothing and do not count. Give the letter on its own.
fact: A Scrabble set has 100 tiles, and two of them are blanks that score nothing.

title: Union Jack
q: British-born drivers who have won the F1 world title, up to 2024
rule: Judged by place of birth in the United Kingdom, not by the team they raced for. Titles from 1950 to 2024 only.
fact: Mike Hawthorn won the 1958 title by a single point over Stirling Moss.

title: Apparatus check
q: Artistic gymnastics apparatus used at the Olympic Games
rule: Count each apparatus once, whichever gender uses it. Trampolining is not an apparatus in this sense.
fact: The balance beam is 5 metres long and only 10 centimetres wide.

traps.Pole vault: Pole vault is an athletics event, not a gymnastics apparatus.
traps.Hurdles: Hurdles are an athletics event, not a gymnastics apparatus.
traps.Javelin: The javelin is an athletics event, not a gymnastics apparatus.

title: Line-up
q: Playing positions in 15-a-side rugby union
rule: Count each position name once. Singular and plural forms both count.
fact: A rugby union side has eight forwards and seven backs on the pitch at once.

traps.Point guard: Point guard is a basketball position.

title: Table colours
q: Ball colours used in a standard snooker frame
rule: Each colour counts once, however many balls of that colour are on the table.
fact: A standard frame uses 22 balls: 15 reds, six colours and the cue ball.
